module_title: Specific Fruit Juices: Exotic and Vegetable Blends

lessons.title: Mango, Papaya, and Guava Juice Processing
lessons.body: Mango, papaya, and guava are abundant in many African countries. To make juice, start with fully ripe, clean fruit. For mango, wash, peel, and slice flesh away from the seed. Use a stainless steel knife to avoid darkening. For papaya, cut in half, scoop out seeds, and peel. For guava, wash and cut off ends, then chop. A good ratio is 1 kg fruit to 500 ml water. Blend fruit with water in a blender or use a pulper. For guava, you may need to strain through a muslin cloth to remove hard seeds. Add 1 teaspoon of lemon juice per litre to prevent browning and enhance flavour. For mango and papaya, you can pasteurize by heating juice to 85Â°C for 30 seconds, then cool quickly. For guava, heating to 90Â°C for 1 minute helps extract more colour and flavour. Sweeten with sugar syrup (1 part sugar to 1 part water) to taste, about 100-150 ml per litre. Bottle in clean, sterilized bottles. Store in refrigerator for up to 5 days, or freeze for longer. In Africa, use local varieties like Kent mango, Solo papaya, and Thai guava. Avoid overripe or bruised fruit. For a smoother juice, use a fine mesh strainer or cheesecloth. You can also blend mango with a little coconut water for a tropical twist. Always taste and adjust sweetness. This process yields about 2 litres of juice from 1 kg fruit. Sell fresh or chilled. Label with production date.

lessons.title: Pomegranate Juice: Extraction and Clarification
lessons.body: Pomegranate juice is prized for its health benefits. In Africa, pomegranates grow in dry regions like Egypt, Morocco, and South Africa. To extract juice, first wash the fruit. Cut off the crown, then score the skin into quarters. Soak in water for 5 minutes to loosen seeds. Break apart in a bowl of water; the seeds sink, and the white pith floats. Skim off pith. Drain seeds. For juice, blend seeds on low speed for 30 secondsâavoid high speed to prevent bitter taste from seed kernels. Strain through a fine mesh sieve or muslin cloth. For clarification, let juice stand in refrigerator for 24 hours; sediment settles. Carefully pour off clear juice. Alternatively, add 1 teaspoon of bentonite clay per litre, stir, let settle, then filter. Another method: heat juice to 70Â°C for 10 seconds, cool, and filter. Clarified juice is clear and ruby-red. Sweeten if needed with sugar syrup (1:1) to taste, about 50-100 ml per litre. Add 1/4 teaspoon citric acid per litre to preserve colour. Pasteurize at 85Â°C for 30 seconds if storing. Bottle in dark glass to protect from light. Store refrigerated for up to 7 days. For a traditional African drink, mix pomegranate juice with a little ginger and honey. Yield: 1 kg seeds gives about 500 ml juice. Use fresh fruit; avoid shriveled skin. This juice is rich in antioxidants. Sell as a premium health juice.

lessons.title: Coconut Water and Coconut Milk Extraction
lessons.body: Coconut water is the clear liquid inside young green coconuts. Coconut milk is made from grated mature coconut flesh. In Africa, coconuts are common in coastal regions like Ghana, Kenya, and Mozambique. For coconut water, choose young, green coconuts. Cut off the top with a heavy knife or machete. Pour water into a clean container. One coconut yields 200-300 ml water. Drink fresh or bottle and refrigerate for up to 2 days. For coconut milk, use mature brown coconuts. Crack open, pry out flesh, and grate finely. For every 1 cup grated coconut, add 1 cup hot water (not boiling). Let sit 10 minutes. Squeeze through muslin cloth or fine strainer. This is first-press milk (thick). Repeat with another 1 cup hot water for second-press (thin). Combine or keep separate. For a richer milk, use 1 cup coconut to 1/2 cup water. To make coconut cream, refrigerate milk; thick cream rises to top. For juice blends, mix coconut water with mango or pineapple. Coconut milk can be used in smoothies. To pasteurize coconut milk, heat to 80Â°C for 5 minutes, stirring. Cool quickly. Bottle in sterilized jars. Store refrigerated for 3-4 days. In Africa, you can add a pinch of salt to enhance flavour. Yield: 1 mature coconut gives about 500 ml milk. Use fresh coconut; avoid moldy or sour smell. Sell coconut water as a natural electrolyte drink.

lessons.title: Vegetable-Fruit Juice Blends for Health
lessons.body: Vegetable-fruit blends are nutritious and popular in African markets. Common vegetables: carrots, beetroot, spinach, cucumber, and tomato. Fruits: orange, pineapple, apple, and mango. Start with 70% vegetable and 30% fruit for a healthy, low-sugar juice. Wash all produce well. Peel carrots, beetroot, and pineapple. For spinach, use leaves only. Chop into small pieces. Use a juicer or blender. If using a blender, add 1 cup water per 2 cups produce, blend, then strain through muslin cloth. For a smoothie, do not strain. Example blend: 2 carrots, 1 beetroot, 1 orange, and 1 cm ginger. This yields about 500 ml. Beetroot gives deep red colour; carrot adds sweetness. Add 1 teaspoon lemon juice per litre to preserve. For green blend: 2 cups spinach, 1 cucumber, 1 green apple, and 1/2 lemon. Sweeten with honey if needed. For tomato blend: 3 tomatoes, 1 carrot, 1 stalk celery, and a pinch of salt. Pasteurize if storing: heat to 85Â°C for 30 seconds. Cool and bottle. Store refrigerated for up to 3 days. In Africa, use local produce like amaranth leaves or moringa. Moringa leaves add protein. Always taste and adjust. Serve chilled. These blends are good for immunity and digestion. Sell in clear bottles to show colour. Label with ingredients and date.

lessons.title: Superfood Juices: Acai, Goji, and Noni
lessons.body: Acai, goji, and noni are exotic superfoods. In Africa, they may be imported as dried powder or juice concentrate. Acai berries are from South America; goji berries from Asia; noni from Pacific. For juice, use 1 tablespoon acai powder or 2 tablespoons goji berries per 500 ml water. For goji, soak dried berries in hot water for 10 minutes, then blend and strain. For noni, use 1 tablespoon noni powder or 30 ml noni concentrate per 500 ml. Blend with 1 cup of a base juice like apple or pineapple to mask strong flavours. Add 1 teaspoon honey or sugar syrup. For a superfood blend: 1 tablespoon acai powder, 1 tablespoon goji powder, 1 teaspoon noni powder, 500 ml coconut water, and 1/2 cup mango. Blend until smooth. Strain if desired. Pasteurize at 80Â°C for 30 seconds if bottling. Store refrigerated for up to 3 days. These juices are expensive; sell in small 250 ml bottles. In Africa, you can source powders from health shops or importers. Always check for authenticity. Use clean equipment. For noni, use ripe fruitâit has a strong smell. Mix with citrus to improve taste. Yield: 500 ml per recipe. These juices are marketed for energy and immunity. Label clearly with ingredients and health claims only if allowed. Keep records.

lessons.title: Melon and Watermelon Juice Production
lessons.body: Melon and watermelon are refreshing and abundant in Africa. For watermelon juice, choose a ripe, heavy melon. Wash, cut in half, and scoop flesh into a blender. Remove seeds if desired. Blend for 30 seconds. Strain through a fine mesh sieve to remove pulp. For every 1 litre juice, add 1 tablespoon lemon juice and 2 tablespoons sugar syrup (optional). Watermelon juice is best fresh; drink within 24 hours. For melon juice, use cantaloupe or honeydew. Peel, remove seeds, and cube. Blend with 1/4 cup water per 2 cups melon. Strain. Add 1 teaspoon lemon juice per litre. For a blend, mix watermelon and melon with a few mint leaves. Pasteurize if storing: heat to 85Â°C for 30 seconds, cool quickly. Bottle in sterilized bottles. Store refrigerated for up to 3 days. In Africa, watermelon is called 'water melon' in some regions. Use a clean knife and board. Avoid overripe melons. Yield: 1 kg watermelon gives about 600 ml juice. For a slushy, freeze juice in ice cube trays, then blend. Sell chilled. Add a pinch of salt to enhance sweetness. For variety, blend watermelon with basil or ginger. Always taste before bottling. Label with date.

quiz.q: What is the recommended ratio of fruit to water when making mango juice?
options: A) 1 kg fruit to 500 ml water
B) 1 kg fruit to 1 litre water
C) 2 kg fruit to 500 ml water
D) 1 kg fruit to 250 ml water
quiz.explanation: The lesson states 1 kg fruit to 500 ml water for mango, papaya, and guava juice.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid blending pomegranate seeds on high speed?
options: A) It makes the juice too sweet
B) It can release bitter flavours from the seeds
C) It causes the juice to foam
quiz.explanation: High speed blending can break the seed kernels and release bitter compounds.

quiz.q: How long should you let pomegranate juice stand in the refrigerator for clarification?
quiz.explanation: The lesson says to let it stand for 24 hours so sediment settles.

quiz.q: What type of coconut is used for coconut water?
quiz.explanation: Coconut water is the clear liquid inside young green coconuts.

quiz.q: How much water is added to 1 cup of grated coconut for first-press coconut milk?
quiz.explanation: The lesson says to add 1 cup hot water to 1 cup grated coconut for first-press milk.

quiz.q: What is the recommended ratio of vegetable to fruit in a healthy blend?
quiz.explanation: The lesson recommends 70% vegetable and 30% fruit for a low-sugar healthy juice.

quiz.q: Which of these is a common vegetable used in African vegetable-fruit blends?
quiz.explanation: Beetroot is listed as a common vegetable for blends, along with carrots, spinach, etc.

quiz.q: How much acai powder is recommended per 500 ml water for superfood juice?
quiz.explanation: The lesson says 1 tablespoon acai powder per 500 ml water.

quiz.q: What should you do with dried goji berries before blending?
options: A) Soak in hot water for 10 minutes
D) Soak in cold water overnight
quiz.explanation: The lesson instructs to soak dried goji berries in hot water for 10 minutes.

quiz.q: Which fruit is recommended to mask the strong flavour of noni?
quiz.explanation: The lesson suggests blending noni with apple or pineapple juice to mask the strong flavour.

quiz.q: What is the yield of juice from 1 kg of watermelon?
quiz.explanation: The lesson states 1 kg watermelon gives about 600 ml juice.

quiz.q: How long can fresh watermelon juice be stored?
quiz.explanation: Watermelon juice is best fresh and should be drunk within 24 hours.

quiz.q: What is added to melon juice to enhance flavour and prevent browning?
quiz.explanation: Lemon juice is added to melon juice for flavour and to prevent browning.

quiz.q: What temperature is recommended for pasteurizing mango juice?
quiz.explanation: The lesson says to pasteurize mango and papaya juice at 85Â°C for 30 seconds.

quiz.q: Which fruit juice requires straining through muslin cloth to remove hard seeds?
quiz.explanation: Guava juice may need straining to remove hard seeds.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of adding bentonite clay to pomegranate juice?
quiz.explanation: Bentonite clay is used as a clarifying agent to settle sediment.

quiz.q: How long can coconut water be stored in the refrigerator?
quiz.explanation: The lesson says coconut water can be refrigerated for up to 2 days.

quiz.q: What is the first step in extracting coconut milk?
options: A) Crack the coconut and grate the flesh
D) Soak the coconut in water
quiz.explanation: To make coconut milk, you first crack the mature coconut and grate the flesh.

quiz.q: Which of these is a recommended green vegetable for juice blends?
quiz.explanation: Spinach is listed as a common green vegetable for blends.

quiz.q: What is the yield of a vegetable-fruit blend using 2 carrots, 1 beetroot, 1 orange, and ginger?
quiz.explanation: The lesson states this blend yields about 500 ml.

quiz.q: Which superfood is originally from the Pacific?
quiz.explanation: Noni is from the Pacific, while acai is from South America and goji from Asia.

quiz.q: How much noni concentrate is recommended per 500 ml water?
quiz.explanation: The lesson says 30 ml noni concentrate per 500 ml water.

quiz.q: What is a good base juice for superfood blends?
quiz.explanation: The lesson recommends apple or pineapple as a base to mask strong flavours.

quiz.q: How should you choose a watermelon for juicing?
options: A) It should be light for its size
B) It should be heavy for its size
C) It should have a green spot
quiz.explanation: A ripe, heavy watermelon is best for juicing.

quiz.q: What can be added to watermelon juice for a slushy?
options: A) Freeze juice in ice cube trays, then blend
quiz.explanation: The lesson suggests freezing juice in ice cube trays and blending for a slushy.

quiz.q: How long can pasteurized melon juice be stored refrigerated?
quiz.explanation: Pasteurized melon juice can be stored refrigerated for up to 3 days.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of adding a pinch of salt to watermelon juice?
quiz.explanation: A pinch of salt enhances the sweetness of watermelon juice.

quiz.q: Which fruit is NOT mentioned in the lesson on mango, papaya, and guava?
quiz.explanation: Pineapple is not mentioned in that lesson; it is mentioned in other lessons.

quiz.q: What is the recommended sugar syrup ratio for sweetening juices?
options: A) 1 part sugar to 2 parts water
B) 1 part sugar to 1 part water
C) 2 parts sugar to 1 part water
D) 1 part sugar to 3 parts water
quiz.explanation: The lesson uses a 1:1 sugar syrup ratio (1 part sugar to 1 part water).

quiz.q: Why is it important to label juice bottles with production date?
options: B) To track freshness and shelf life
D) To comply with tax laws
quiz.explanation: Labeling with date helps track freshness and ensure quality.
